action.description: Action object MUST contain a field `submission`, and MAY contain arbitrary additional information.

actTimeout.description: Maximum runtime (seconds) to obtain an action from an agent.

episodeSteps.description: Maximum number of steps in the episode.

includeLegalActions.description: If true, include legalActions and legalActionStrings in observations. Defaults to false since these can be derived from serializedGameAndState.

initialActions.description: Actions applied to initial state before play begins to set up starting position.

loadPresetHands.description: Repeated poker only. Load preset hand chance actions from preset_hands.jsonl.

openSpielGameName.description: The short_name of the OpenSpiel game to load.

openSpielGameParameters.description: Game parameters for Open Spiel game.

openSpielGameString.description: The full game string including parameters.

presetHands.description: Repeated poker only. List of per-hand chance action sequences to use instead of random chance.

runTimeout.description: Maximum runtime (seconds) of an episode (not necessarily DONE).

seed.description: Integer currently only used for selecting starting position.

useImage.description: If true, indicates the observation is intended to be rendered as an image. Note that currently the agent harness is responsible for the actual rendering; no image is passed in the observation.

useOpenings.description: Whether to start from a position in an opening book.

currentPlayer.description: ID of player whose turn it is.

legalActionStrings.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action strings. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

legalActions.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action integers. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

openSpielGameName.description: Short name of the OpenSpiel game.

playerId.description: ID of the agent receiving this observation.

serializedGameAndState.description: Enables reconstructing the Game and State objects.

remainingOverageTime.description: Total remaining banked time (seconds) that can be used in excess of per-step actTimeouts -- agent is disqualified with TIMEOUT status when this drops below 0.

The center column is the highest-value position on the board, offering the maximum number of potential lines (horizontal, vertical, and both diagonals). Occupying column 3 immediately prevents that, places o at height 2 in the most contested area, and keeps the position balanced for future threats. Thus, column 3 is the optimal move.

action.thoughts:
### Reasoning
The current board has Player X's piece at the bottom of column 3 (row 5) and Player O's piece stacked on top in the same column (row 4). All other positions are empty. This is an early-game position where no immediate wins or threats exist.

As Player X, the goal is to make the optimal move to position for a win, assuming perfect play. In Connect 4 (6x7 board, 4 to win), the center column (3) is key for control. With O stacking on X's first piece, the optimal strategy is not to stack again in column 3, as that places a piece higher up without creating immediate connections or forcing O to respond, and it wastes the opportunity to build a strong base in the bottom row.

Instead, the best move is to play in an adjacent column (2 or 4) at the bottom row to create two connected X pieces horizontally (e.g., row 5, columns 3 and 4). This sets up a potential for quickly building to three in a row with both ends open, which would be unstoppable (O can't block both ends in one turn). This forces O to block the extension (e.g., in column 5 or 1), giving X initiative and preventing O from safely building in the center column.

Columns 2 and 4 are symmetric and equally optimal. I choose column 2 (the lower index) for specificity.

Final Answer: 2

action.thoughts:
### Reasoning

The current board state shows Player X with pieces in columns 2 and 3 at row 5, forming a horizontal pair. Player O has a vertical pair in column 3 at rows 3 and 4.

No immediate winning move exists for X, as adding a single piece cannot form 4 in a row.

However, placing an X in column 4 drops to row 5, creating a horizontal 3 in a row (columns 2-4 at row 5). This threatens a win in either column 1 (completing columns 1-4) or column 5 (completing columns 2-5), both open.

O can block only one threat per turn. If O blocks one, X completes the other on the next turn, winning. If O ignores and builds their vertical in column 3 (creating a 3 in a row threatening a future win), X immediately completes one horizontal 4, winning before O's next turn.

Placing in column 1 also creates a similar double threat (threatening columns 0 and 4). Both moves force a win for X assuming optimal play.

In case of ties, prefer the move closer to the center (column 3). Column 4 is closer (|4-3|=1) than column 1 (|1-3|=2).

Thus, the optimal move is column 4.

Final Answer: 4
